ex.s: According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.

ex.s: Benjamin could read only a little,having been a poor student.But he later said,”Those two books were my companions by day,and under my pillow at night.”While it is likely that he understood very little of the books,they were his introduction to classical paintings.The nine-year-old boy decided then that he would be an artist.
ex.t: 本杰明只读过一点书，因为他曾是个差学生。但他后来说：“那两本书白天是我的伙伴，晚上就在我的枕头下。”虽然他很可能几乎看不懂那些书，但它们是他接触古典绘画的入门。这个九岁男孩当时就下定决心要成为一名艺术家。

ex.s: AI will affect us all, and if you only read one book on the subject, this is it.
ex.t: 人工智能将影响我们所有人，如果你只读一本关于这个主题的书，那就是这本。

ex.t: 大家都安静地等待，看谁会被叫起来大声朗读自己的段落。

ex.s: When you see the capitalized “WHO” in a medical report, do you read it as the “who” in “Who’s that?

ex.s: ●Read it; hear it; be it!
ex.t: ●读它；听它；成为它！

ex.s: Each subject got eight reviews to read: a balanced set of two positive fake, two positive real, two negative fake and two negative real, presented in a random order.
ex.t: 每位受试者读了八条评论：均衡地包含两条正面虚假、两条正面真实、两条负面虚假和两条负面真实，以随机顺序呈现。

ex.s: Whaley says the project is about more than just learning to read and speak in public.
ex.t: 惠利说，这个项目不只是关于学习在公开场合朗读和说话。

ex.s: The more dispassionate that negative write-up, the more likely it was to take the reader in.
ex.t: 负面评论写得越冷静克制，就越容易让读者信以为真。

ex.s: When scanning a text, you read it quickly in order to find a specific piece of information.
ex.t: 在扫描一个文本时，您会快速读取，以便找到一个特定的信息片段。

ex.s: The writing in magazines also tends to be easy to read, especially if it is a children's publication.
ex.t: 杂志的写作也往往易读，尤其是儿童刊物。

ex.s: Reading history is an amazing experience because it enables us to reflect on the social and economic life of the people living long time ago.
ex.t: 读史是一种奇妙的体验，因为它让我们得以反思很久以前人们的社会与经济生活。

ex.s: Long before reading and writing became widely spread and available, oral storytelling had already been a form that the wisdom and knowledge of the people were passed down from elders to children.
ex.t: 早在读写广泛普及之前，口头讲故事就已是人们将智慧和知识从长辈传给孩子的一种形式。

ex.s: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
ex.t: 最终读到的，是我们学会像苏格拉底一样发问、像梭罗一样观察、像叔本华一样倾听、像尼采一样无怨无悔。

ex.s: The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties.
ex.t: 印刷和数字阅读结果之间的差异部分与纸张的物理特性有关。

ex.s: Feature stories typically start with a "hook" that gets the interest of the reader.
ex.t: 特写故事通常以一个能吸引读者兴趣的"钩子"开头。

ex.s: Later, a second student wanted to read with him, then a third.
ex.t: 后来，第二个学生想和他一起读书，接着是第三个。

ex.s: All the kids went to the teacher asking, “Can I read with Mr Herman?”
ex.t: 所有孩子都跑去问老师："我能和赫尔曼先生一起读书吗？"

ex.s: Yet， now that I'm growing and the world I once knew as being so simple is becoming more complex， I find myself needing a way to escape． By opening a novel， I can leave behind my burdens and enter into a wonderful and mysterious world where I am now a new character． In these worlds I can become anyone． I don't have to write down what happened or what technique the author was using when he or she wrote this． I just read to relax．
ex.t: 然而，随着我渐渐长大，曾经以为如此简单的世界变得越来越复杂，我发现自己需要一种逃避的方式。打开一本小说，我就能抛开烦恼，进入一个奇妙而神秘的世界，在那里我成为一个新的角色。在这些世界里我可以成为任何人。我不必记下发生了什么，也不必分析作者写作时运用了什么技巧。我阅读只是为了放松。

ex.s: Magazine articles can provide reluctant readers with a lively, breezy writing style that can inspire them to read more.
ex.t: 杂志文章能以生动、轻松的写作风格为不情愿的读者提供灵感，鼓励他们多阅读。

ex.s: We're taught to read because it's necessary for much of human understanding． Reading is a vital part of my life． Reading satisfies my desire to keep learning． And I've found that the possibilities that lie within books are limitless．
ex.t: 我们被教导阅读，因为这对于人类理解的许多内容来说是必要的。阅读是我生活中不可或缺的一部分。阅读满足了我不断学习的渴望。而且我发现，书中蕴含的可能性是无限的。

ex.s: People now rarely have the patience to read.
ex.t: 如今人们很少有阅读的耐心。

ex.s: The light，about one-thousandth of the amount needed to read by，is just a start.
ex.t: 这种光约为阅读所需光强的千分之一，只是一个开端。

ex.s: I was willing; I would do anything to read.
ex.t: 我愿意；为了读书我什么都愿意做。

ex.s: “Eudora is nine years old and has my permission to read any book she wants from the shelves, children or adults,” Mother said.
ex.t: "Eudora九岁了，我允许她阅读书架上任何她想读的书，无论是儿童读物还是成人读物，"妈妈说。

ex.s: Desire to read.
ex.t: 阅读的渴望。

ex.s: Students should read the list with their parents / carers, and select two activities they would like to do.
ex.t: 学生应和家长/监护人一起阅读清单，并选择两项他们想做的活动。

ex.s: Data shows that kids and teens who do read frequently, compared to infrequent readers, have more books in the home, more books purchased for them, parents who read more often, and parents who set aside time for them to read.
ex.t: 数据显示，与不常阅读的孩子和青少年相比，经常阅读的孩子和青少年家里有更多的书，为他们购买的书籍更多，父母阅读更频繁，并且父母会为他们留出阅读时间。

ex.s: How should parents encourage their children to read more?
ex.t: 家长应该如何鼓励孩子多读书？

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 每个人都是这样学会阅读的。我们从句子开始，然后是段落，再然后是故事。这似乎是一段永无止境的旅程，但即使作为一个六岁的女孩，我也意识到学会阅读能打开许多扇门。当妈妈说：“C-A-N-D-Y藏在最上面的架子上”时，我知道糖果在哪里。我在阅读上的进步激发了我的好奇心，我想知道一切。我经常叫妈妈开慢一点，这样我就能读出我们路过的所有路标。

ex.s: Do you ever get to the train station and realize you forgot to bring something to read?
ex.t: 你有没有过到了火车站才发现忘了带读物的时候？

ex.s: One of the    60   (effect) ways to build vocabulary is to read good books.
ex.t: 建立词汇量最有效（60）的方法之一就是读好书。

ex.s: But something about quantum computing makes it especially prone to hype, Johnson suggests, perhaps because “‘quantum’ stands for something cool you shouldn’t be able to understand.” And that brings me back to Taylor, who suggested that I read his book Q for Quantum.
